venue.name: U'mista Cultural Centre
venue.description: U'mista Cultural Centre is a Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw museum and cultural centre at 1 Front Street in Alert Bay, run by the U'mista Cultural Society. The present facility opened in November 1980 and the focus of the permanent collection is the Potlatch Collection, masks and other regalia confiscated after an illegal potlatch in 1921 and returned to the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw over the decades that followed. Other permanent exhibits cover the traditional ethnobiology of the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw, the origin stories of the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw villages, and historical and contemporary objects, alongside travelling exhibits. The centre also runs an art gallery and gift shop, private guided tours and a weekly drop-in tour in summer.
venue.address: #1 Front Street, Alert Bay, British Columbia, Canada V0N 1A0
venue.hours_notes: Monday to Friday 9:00 am - 5:00 pm. Closed STAT Holidays.
venue.seasonal_notes: A weekly drop-in tour runs on select Saturdays in summer, and Tʼsasała Cultural Group performances run throughout July and August at the ʼNa̱mg̱is Big House.

programs.name: Private guided tour
programs.description: The centre books private guided tours of the Cultural Centre, where a guide talks about the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw people, the culture and the objects on display. Artist demonstrations away from the centre and totem pole talks beside the ʼNa̱mǥis Original Burial Grounds can also be scheduled. The price, the length, the group size and how much notice is needed are not published. The tourism coordinator handles scheduling and pricing.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the galleries with a guide and look at the masks and other regalia of the Potlatch Collection while the guide talks about them. If it is arranged in advance, the group can also watch an artist working, or stand beside the totem poles at the ʼNa̱mǥis Original Burial Grounds and hear about them.
programs.our_note: Nothing about this tour is priced on the site, so the first email decides your budget. Ask what it costs per child and per adult, how long the tour runs, and how many children they will take at once. Their published opening times are weekdays only, so settle the day before you plan anything else around it.
programs.practical_summary: The address, the phone number and the person who books tours are published, and so are the walk-in admission prices. Nothing is stated about washrooms, somewhere to eat, how many adults have to come, or what the tour itself costs, so plan on a phone call.
programs.evidence: Book a private guided tour of our Cultural Centre and experience and learn about the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw people, culture and artifacts.

programs.name: Self-guided visit
programs.description: The centre is open to the public. Admission is $15 for adults, $12 for seniors and students, $5 for youth aged 8 to 18, and free for children under 8. A family rate of $30 covers 2 adults and 4 children under 18. GST is not included, and admission is free to members and to Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw. No group rate, school rate or group booking route is published for a self-guided visit.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the galleries at their own pace and look at the masks and other regalia of the Potlatch Collection, along with exhibits on the traditional ethnobiology of the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw, the origin stories of the villages, and historical and contemporary objects.
programs.our_note: Children under 8 come in free and the $5 rate only starts at age 8, so a preschool group would mostly be paying for its adults. There is no group rate on the site, so ask whether a class is charged per head or quoted as a whole. Prices are before tax.
programs.practical_summary: The admission prices, the address and the opening times are published, and the visit is indoors. Washrooms, somewhere for a group to eat, and whether a group has to book ahead are not stated anywhere, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $5 rate is for youth aged 8 to 18. Children under 8 are free. A family rate of $30 covers 2 adults and 4 children under 18. Admission is free to members and to Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw.

programs.name: Weekly drop-in tour
programs.description: A one hour drop-in tour runs from 10 am to 11 am on select Saturdays in summer at $20 per person, which does not include admission. The page lists July dates of the 11th, 18th and 26th but does not give a year. Places are first come first served and the centre recommends arriving early to secure a spot. There is no way to reserve it for a group.
programs.our_note: This one is first come first served, so you cannot hold spots for a class. The $20 sits on top of admission, which makes it the dearest way in for a group. If you want a set time and a known price, ask about a private tour instead.
programs.practical_summary: The price, the day, the hour and how places are allocated are all published. What the tour covers, how big a group can join and whether it runs past July are not, so ask before you count on it.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission is not included in the $20.
programs.evidence: starting select Saturdays this summer for $20 per person (not including admission)

programs.name: Tʼsasała Cultural Group performance
programs.description: Traditional Kwakwaka'wakw dances performed by the Tʼsasała Dance Group throughout July and August at the ʼNa̱mg̱is Big House, on Saturday afternoons. The performers are local children and youth. Tickets are available at U'mista. The ticket price, the start time and how long a performance runs are not published, and the Big House is a separate building from the Cultural Centre.
programs.what_children_do: Watch local children and youth perform traditional Kwakwaka'wakw songs and dances in the ʼNa̱mg̱is Big House, including the Hamatʼsa, which the group describes as the most important of their sacred dances.
programs.our_note: This happens in the Big House rather than inside the centre, so treat it as a second stop and not part of a museum visit. Nothing is published about the price, the start time or how long it lasts, so ask when you buy tickets. It runs in July and August only, which puts it outside most school terms.
programs.practical_summary: The season, the day and the place are published, and tickets are sold at the centre. The price, the start time and how long it runs are not, so ask before you plan around it.
